title: Innocence
full_review:
"Innocence" (Leisure Time and Home Vision Entertainment) is a strange but intriguing tale set within the curious confines of an all-girls boarding school cut off from the outside world. Students arrive as small children in coffins, are quickly indoctrinated into the school's strict rules -- including those forbidding escape -- are instructed in natural science and dance, and then released upon reaching puberty.

The only adults are a pair of caretaking crones and two young teachers -- Mademoiselle Eva (Marion Cotillard) and Mademoiselle Edith (Helene de Fougerolles) -- so the senior students look after the younger ones.

The story follows 6-year-old new arrival Iris (Zoe Auclair) and Bianca (Berangere Haubruge), an older girl who takes her under her wing and who, nightly, sneaks off into the woods to perform in bizarre ballets for the school's shadowy patrons.

Then there are those creepy subterranean tunnels ... .

Directed by French filmmaker Lucile Hadzihalilovic, the visually haunting picture conveys a sense of both innocence and dread, but its laggard pacing and plotless narrative undercut its feminist-flavored pretensions of social commentary concerning the role of women in society.

Subtitles.

The film contains a brief sensually suggestive scene. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. Not rated by the Motion Picture Association of America.
